items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: I was playing with Pierron on band number two with Hippolyte Charles.

ctx.x: He was with Pierron on trombone for years. Tell him he was with Pierron.

He used to be with Pierron on trombone a long time. Johnny Lindsey. Yeah. And he was this bright fella? Yeah, this slender tall brown skin fella. Yeah. He went to Chicago. Oh, yeah. Well, maybe he was playing with Romeo with Pierron, but I was playing with Pierron on band number two with Hippolyte Charles. You got him, ain't ya? Mm-hmm. Yeah. I was playing with him. But the doctor stopped Hippolyte Charles from playing on a guy that had bad hearts and
the, uh, let's see, who else would be with Robeshoe?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: I wasn't playing with him then, you know. I played with him after they'd get that up, him and Clarence William, you know.

ctx.x: P-Ron and Williams. Oh, you mean how long did I? Oh, I didn't play with them then. They used to go there, you know. And when we'd go off, well he'd give me a stack of music to sell, you know. He'd go to the streets, folks, and Texas, all them places, and Oklahoma, you know. And he'd give me a bunch like that to sell for, you know. But I wasn't at the place, I just used to go there sometime. I wasn't playing with him then, you know. I played with him after they'd get that up, him and Clarence William, you know.…
How did you sell that music?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: Like Lewis DeMille, Joe Howard, and uh, uh, uh, Charles Williams, and uh, Perron. All them fellas used to see how I could read it. They'd just help me out.

ctx.x: He said who was it couldn't read?

Named Pinn? Pinn, Pinn and uh. Oh Pinn? Pinn. Pinn. Pinn he couldn't read. He couldn't read or Lee. Yeah. Zeb kept by telling Buddy to read. Lee could spell a little bit Lee Cotty but maybe Lee was something like me you know. I always kept with musicians and learning more with him and learning under there. And that's where I was. I was taking about four or five lessons with different teachers you know. I'd tell about, that'd take about five or six months. You know a lesson. But all I'd learn from them fellas…
Did Buddy and Louis Armstrong ever buck? No.
